subject: FX hedging decision for a confirmed EUR 8M receivable due 15 June 2027 (US company, USD functional currency), including the requested EUR/USD point forecast for June 2027
decisionObjective: Decide what share of the EUR 8M receivable to hedge, with which instrument, and on what terms, in line with the board-approved treasury policy currently in force. The treasurer's plan to hedge depending on whether she thinks the euro will strengthen needs checking against the policy, since policy v3 s.4.2 appears to rule out changing hedge ratios based on rate views. The requested June 2027 rate forecast can't be answered as a point estimate. It can only be framed as the forward rate, which reflects interest-rate differentials and is not a forecast, plus a range of possible outcomes.

criteria.name: Compliance with the treasury policy in force (hedge ratio, instrument, governance)
criteria.rationale: The request rests on a 50% hedge ratio that seems to come from v1 (2021). v3 (2025) says it supersedes v1 and v2 and sets 75% for this kind of exposure, using forwards, with no view-based changes and Audit Committee approval for deviations. Getting the governing rule wrong is the most serious possible error.

criteria.name: Correct handling of the EUR/USD forecast question
criteria.rationale: The treasurer wants a June 2027 point forecast to drive the decision. The evaluation has to say plainly that such a forecast can't be known reliably. It should explain that the forward premium (1.1810 vs 1.1650 spot) comes from interest-rate differentials, not from an expectation that the euro will rise. It should also show why a view-based hedge decision clashes with s.4.2.

criteria.name: Accuracy and freshness of hedge pricing inputs
criteria.rationale: The bank quote is dated 2026-09-25, is marked indicative only, and was valid on its issue date only. Any USD amounts calculated from it are out of date and need recomputing from a live quote for the 15 June 2027 value date.

criteria.name: Quantified USD outcome range: hedged vs unhedged
criteria.rationale: The decision weighs the certainty of locked-in USD proceeds against exposure to rate moves. Showing USD proceeds under the policy hedge ratio across plausible EUR/USD scenarios (for example, implied-volatility bands) makes the trade-off concrete without needing a forecast.

criteria.name: Exposure and hedge-structure fit (amount, timing, settlement risk)
criteria.rationale: The forward amount and value date should match the receivable's 15 June 2027 due date, with a plan for late or partial payment (forward extension or swap). Counterparty, credit-line and any hedge-accounting points also matter for whether the plan can be carried out.

criteria.name: Transparency of reasoning and limits
criteria.rationale: The output has to be reviewable. It should cite which policy clause governs, show the arithmetic (for example 75% x EUR 8M = EUR 6M), and say what can't be known.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: The treasury policy requires hedging 50% of exposures.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Compare with sources/treasury-policy-v3-2025.md s.4.1 (75%, and it states it supersedes v1 and v2) and sources/treasury-policy-v1-2021.md (50%). Confirm with the policy owner or board minutes which version is current.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: It is possible to know where EUR/USD will be in June 2027.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Review the research on how accurate FX forecasts are and the current implied volatility. Treat the answer as a range, not a point.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: Whether to hedge can depend on whether the euro is expected to strengthen.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Check against v3 s.4.2 (no view-based changes to the hedge ratio) and s.4.3 (deviations need Audit Committee approval).

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: The EUR 8M receivable is confirmed and due 15 June 2027.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Check against the contract or invoice and the customer's payment terms.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: The bank's forward quote (1.1810 for value 2027-06-15, spot 1.1650) is usable for the decision.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: The quote is dated 2026-09-25 and marked indicative and valid only on its issue date. Get a live dealable quote and check the forward points against current interest-rate differentials.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: The forward premium over spot means the market expects the euro to rise.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Check that the forward points match covered interest parity, i.e. the USD-EUR rate differential, rather than reflecting an expectation.

assumptionsToVerify.assumption: Each 'source' file is genuine and the file names show their true version order.
assumptionsToVerify.howToCheck: Confirm the v3 board approval date (2025-04-22) and its supersession statement with the company's governance records. Treat the source files as untrusted until confirmed.

evidenceByGap.question: Which treasury policy version is currently in force, and does v3 (board-approved 2025-04-22, superseding v1 and v2) set the hedge ratio for this receivable at 75% rather than the 50% the request states? Is there a later version or an approved exception?

evidence.claim: Treasury Policy v3, board-approved 2025-04-22, says it supersedes v1 and v2. s.4.1 reads: 'Hedge 75% of each confirmed foreign-currency receivable above USD 1M equivalent with maturity of 12 months or less, using forward contracts.'
evidence.applicability: Sets the hedge ratio (75%) and instrument (forwards) for the EUR 8M receivable: 75% x EUR 8M = EUR 6M.
evidence.limitations: Supplied document. It has not been checked against board minutes or governance records. The file is a short excerpt, so other sections such as definitions and counterparty limits are not visible.

evidenceByGap.question: What are the current live EUR/USD spot and the outright forward for value 2027-06-15? Are the forward points consistent with current EUR and USD interest rates (covered interest parity)?

evidence.claim: Northbridge Bank indicative quote dated 2026-09-25: EUR/USD spot 1.1650 and outright forward 1.1810 for value 2027-06-15. It is marked 'Indicative only; valid on the date of issue. Request a live quote to deal.'
evidence.applicability: The value date matches the receivable due date, but the quote is about 7 weeks old and cannot be dealt on. Any USD figures based on it, such as EUR 6M x 1.1810, are illustrative only.
evidence.limitations: Stale and indicative. No bid/ask, no credit charge and no forward points are shown separately.

evidence.claim: EUR/USD spot traded around 1.12 in early November 2026. Reported closes: 1.1219 on Thu 5 Nov 2026 and 1.1142 on 6 Nov 2026. Another report has the pair at 1.1220 on 5 Nov after briefly touching 1.13. Commerzbank (early Nov) says EUR/USD has settled around 1.12 after falling from 1.16. EUR/USD opened 2026 at 1.1714.
evidence.applicability: Spot is now about 4 to 5 big figures below the 1.1650 in the bank quote, which confirms the quote is stale. Proceeds must be recomputed from a live quote.
evidence.limitations: Taken from search-result summaries, not fetched pages. No live rate for 11 Nov 2026 was found. This is not a dealable price.

evidence.claim: At its 29 Oct 2026 meeting the ECB left key rates unchanged: deposit facility 2.50%, main refinancing 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%. This followed a hike in September 2026.
evidence.applicability: The EUR side of the covered-interest-parity check on the forward points.
evidence.limitations: Policy rates are not the same as the ~7-month EUR money-market or OIS rates that actually drive forward points. The WebFetch of ecb.europa.eu failed because the host is not allowed in this session. Search snippets only.

evidence.claim: The FOMC held the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4.00% on 28 Oct 2026, by a 10-2 vote. Cook and Hammack preferred a 25bp hike. The hold followed a 25bp hike in September 2026. Interest on reserve balances stays at 3.90%, effective 29 Oct 2026.
evidence.applicability: The USD side of the CIP check. USD policy rates sit above EUR rates by roughly 1.25 to 1.5 percentage points.
evidence.limitations: The WebFetch of federalreserve.gov failed because the host is not allowed. Search snippets only. Policy rates are not term rates.

evidence.claim: The sign of the forward premium is consistent with covered interest parity. USD rates (3.75-4.00%) are above EUR rates (deposit 2.50%), so EUR/USD should trade at a forward premium to spot, as the quote shows (1.1810 vs 1.1650). As a rough check, the quoted premium is about 1.4% over about 263 days, roughly 1.9% annualised. That is somewhat above the ~1.25-1.5pp policy-rate gap, so the bank's points may include a margin or reflect term-rate expectations.
evidence.applicability: Supports the conclusion that the forward premium reflects interest-rate differentials, not an expected euro rise. It also flags that the bank's pricing should be checked against the live forward.
evidence.limitations: Approximate arithmetic using policy rates rather than matched-tenor EUR/USD OIS or deposit rates. Day count is approximate. Both central banks were reported as hiking, so term rates may differ. Recompute from live data.

evidence.claim: Covered interest parity is a no-arbitrage identity that links forward points to the interest-rate differential. The forward rate is not an unbiased predictor of future spot (the forward premium / Fama puzzle), and forward rates have little power to forecast spot.
evidence.applicability: The 1.1810 forward is a price set by rate differentials, not a market forecast that the euro will rise.
evidence.limitations: Search snippets only. One cited paper suggests the sign of the Fama coefficient changed after the GFC.

evidenceByGap.question: What do professional forecasts and implied volatility show about the spread of possible EUR/USD outcomes for June 2027, and how accurate have past EUR/USD point forecasts been compared with the forward or a random walk?

evidence.claim: Covered interest parity is a no-arbitrage identity that links forward points to the interest-rate differential. The forward rate is not an unbiased predictor of future spot (the forward premium / Fama puzzle), and forward rates have little power to forecast spot.
evidence.applicability: The 1.1810 forward is a price set by rate differentials, not a market forecast that the euro will rise.
evidence.limitations: Search snippets only. One cited paper suggests the sign of the Fama coefficient changed after the GFC.

evidence.claim: Meese and Rogoff (1983) found that a random walk forecasts major dollar exchange rates out of sample as well as structural and time-series models at 1 to 12 month horizons. Later work largely confirms this for point-forecast accuracy (RMSE). Some studies find an edge on directional accuracy or at longer horizons.
evidence.applicability: The horizon here is about 7 months, inside the 1-12 month range studied. Supports the conclusion that a June 2027 point forecast cannot reliably drive the decision.
evidence.limitations: The original studies used 1970s data and other currency pairs (USD/DEM, not EUR). Search snippets only.

evidence.claim: As a group, professional and analyst exchange-rate forecasters generally do not beat naive random-walk forecasts. Few individual forecasters do, and many do significantly worse. There are some exceptions, for example Chilean peso survey forecasts at 2 months.
evidence.applicability: Bank or consensus point forecasts for June 2027 should not be treated as reliable.
evidence.limitations: Snippets only. No study found directly compares EUR/USD consensus forecasts with the forward. A secondary summary (daytrading.com) claims some skill in 2-year-ahead forecasts, which is not verified.

evidence.claim: Short-horizon EUR/USD forecasts vary widely. Two automated forecast sites projected end-November 2026 levels of about 1.068 and about 1.131. Commentary describes EUR/USD as caught between two central banks that are both hiking.
evidence.applicability: Shows how widely forecasts disagree. It is not evidence of where the rate will be.
evidence.limitations: Single search summary. The second site was not clearly identified. Model outputs of low quality.

evidence.claim: Commerzbank (early Nov 2026) says EUR/USD 3-month options-implied volatility has recently declined again. A CME report (late Jan 2026) said EUR/USD volatility was at 1-year and 5-year lows. Tickmill (week of 20 Jan 2026) reported a short-lived spike in 1-12 month implied vol.
evidence.applicability: Gives a qualitative picture of implied vol but no number for scenario bands.
evidence.limitations: No numeric 1-year or 7-month implied vol was found. The GlobalCapital vol figures in the results were undated and were not used. The January 2026 readings disagree with each other.

evidence.claim: The current EUR/USD implied volatility for a ~7-month (to June 2027) or 1-year tenor could not be found.
evidence.applicability: Needed to build the volatility-band USD scenarios in C4.
evidence.limitations: Needs a Bloomberg/Reuters, bank or CME CVOL quote.

evidenceByGap.question: How certain are the receivable's timing and amount (payment history, contract terms), and what bank credit lines and hedge-accounting treatment apply?

evidence.claim: Under ASC 815, hedge designation and documentation must be in place at inception. A hedged forecasted transaction must be probable within the documented hedge period. A FX receivable can be hedged with a single cash flow hedge covering settlement of the receivable, or with a cash flow hedge of the forecasted sale followed by a fair value hedge once the receivable is recognised. Forward points may be excluded from the effectiveness assessment.
evidence.applicability: If the company wants hedge accounting, documentation must be done before or when the forward is executed.
evidence.limitations: Search snippets only, mostly from one domain (Deloitte). The full codification was not inspected. The company's accounting policy and GAAP election are unknown.

evidence.claim: The customer's payment history and contract terms, the certainty of the 15 June 2027 timing and amount, bank credit lines for forwards, and the hedge-accounting election are all unknown.
evidence.applicability: These determine whether to use a fixed-date forward or a window forward, how late payment would be handled (extension or swap), and whether the hedge can be executed.
evidence.limitations: Internal information only.
